meta_cites_federal_law_008.answer:
A military exigency leave may be taken because of a qualifying exigency, as defined by federal regulations, arising out of the fact that the spouse, or a son, daughter, or parent of the employee is on active duty (or has been notified of an impending call or order to active duty) in the Armed forces in support of a contingency operation.
To the extent possible, employees are required to substitute accrued paid leave, including any paid vacation and personal, state, and local leave, for an equivalent portion of the 12 week period of FMLA leave, and the amount of time taken for paid leaves shall be deducted from the 12 weeks for leave available under the FMLA.
Compensatory time (comp time) used for an FMLA qualifying event may be counted against an employee’s 12-week leave entitlement.
